summary:
SafeHaven is a bilingual (Arabic and English) earthquake awareness app that helps people understand natural hazards and prepare for emergencies. It combines Earth data from USGS, NASA EONET, Open-Meteo, and GNSS with NASA-ISRO NISAR radar scene information. Through interactive maps and city search, users can explore recorded earthquakes, natural events, weather conditions, and GNSS station movement.
The working prototype includes adjustable earthquake search settings, weather checks, emergency information, an offline-ready app shell, and 5- and ten-minute preparedness drills. It also presents a transparent Attention Index that combines atmospheric and seismic signals to highlight changing conditions. This index is for awareness only: it is not a probability, does not predict earthquakes, and is not an official warning.
SafeHaven introduces a future safer-room design concept for protection during earthquakes and related hazards. Its NISAR section displays real radar scenes and marks provisional data. The app does not publish unverified displacement measurements or use raw radar phase for alerts. Simulations are clearly labelled and never presented as real alerts.
By combining accessible Earth data, bilingual information, interactive features, and preparedness tools, SafeHaven aims to make Earth science easier to understand and help communities become more informed and prepared for natural hazards. It does not replace official warnings or instructions from local authorities....
details:
SafeHaven is a bilingual earthquake awareness and preparedness web application designed to help communities understand natural hazards and prepare for emergencies. It combines real Earth observation data from NASA EONET, NASA-ISRO NISAR, USGS, Open-Meteo, and the Nevada Geodetic Laboratory.
Users can search for cities worldwide, explore interactive maps, view recorded earthquakes, monitor natural events and weather conditions, and examine simplified GNSS station movement. The application includes adjustable earthquake search settings, emergency information, an offline-ready app shell, and five- and ten-minute preparedness countdown drills.
SafeHaven also features an Attention Index that combines atmospheric and seismic signals to highlight changing environmental conditions. It is designed for awareness and does not predict earthquakes or replace official alerts.
Another important part of the project is a future safer-room design concept intended to improve protection during earthquakes and related hazards. The team also explores NASA NISAR radar scenes while clearly identifying provisional data and avoiding unsupported scientific claims.
We focused on accessibility through Arabic and English interfaces, transparency in data sources, and responsible communication of scientific limitations. Our goal is to make Earth science more accessible and help families and communities become better informed and prepared for natural disasters.
